**Refined prompt:** Diagnose why an expired JWT from the mobile client returns `500` instead of `401` on this NestJS RealWorld API, answering as a security-minded engineer on this codebase — cite the exact failing line as file:line, name the root cause rather than the symptom, fix it at one source instead of per call site, and state the blast radius, whether existing data is already wrong, and how to verify.

## Root cause

`src/user/auth.middleware.ts:17`

```ts
const decoded: any = jwt.verify(token, SECRET);
```

`jwt.verify` throws `TokenExpiredError` on an expired token. `TokenExpiredError` extends `Error`, **not** `HttpException` — and Nest's exception layer only translates `HttpException` into a status code. Anything else becomes `500 Internal Server Error`. There is no global filter to catch it: `src/main.ts:5-21` never calls `useGlobalFilters`.

The proof that the mechanism is otherwise fine is two lines below and two lines above the failure: `auth.middleware.ts:21` and `auth.middleware.ts:28` throw `HttpException(..., HttpStatus.UNAUTHORIZED)` and reach the client as a clean 401. Line 17 is the only path out of this middleware that escapes as a raw `Error`. So the root cause is not "auth is broken" — it's **one untranslated error type on one line**.

The same untranslated `jwt.verify` exists at two more sites:

- `src/user/user.decorator.ts:15` — the optional-auth path. On a guarded route the early return at `user.decorator.ts:8-10` means this never runs; it only fires on **unguarded** routes that still take `@User()`. In this repo that is exactly one route: `GET /profiles/:username` (`src/profile/profile.controller.ts:18-21`), which is not in `ProfileModule`'s middleware list (`src/profile/profile.module.ts:22` guards only `profiles/:username/follow`).
- `src/shared/base.controller.ts:12` — same bug, but **dead code**: grepping `BaseController` across `src/` returns only its own declaration, nothing extends it.

**Why it surfaces now, not at launch.** `UserService.generateJWT()` sets `exp` to today + 60 days (`src/user/user.service.ts:103-114`). The bug has been there since day one but is unreachable until a token is 60 days old. Mobile is the first client to hit it because it persists the login token and runs for months; a web session re-logs in long before expiry. Note `buildUserRO` mints a *fresh* 60-day token on every `GET /user` (`src/user/user.service.ts:122`) — so any mobile build that ignores the refreshed token in that response walks into the cliff exactly 60 days after install, while a build that stores it rolls forward indefinitely. That's likely why this looks like it started suddenly for one cohort.

## The fix

One shared translation point, so no future `jwt.verify` call site can re-introduce it. New file `src/shared/verify-token.ts`:

```ts
import { HttpException, HttpStatus } from '@nestjs/common';
import * as jwt from 'jsonwebtoken';
import { SECRET } from '../config';

export function verifyToken(token: string): any {
  try {
    return jwt.verify(token, SECRET);
  } catch (err) {
    throw new HttpException('Token expired or invalid.', HttpStatus.UNAUTHORIZED);
  }
}
```

Then the two live call sites become one-line imports:

```diff
--- src/user/auth.middleware.ts:17
-      const decoded: any = jwt.verify(token, SECRET);
+      const decoded: any = verifyToken(token);

--- src/user/user.decorator.ts:15
-    const decoded: any = jwt.verify(token[1], SECRET);
+    const decoded: any = verifyToken(token[1]);
```

This covers `TokenExpiredError`, `JsonWebTokenError` (tampered payload, wrong signature, malformed) and `NotBeforeError` in one place — all four are "we could not establish who you are", all four are 401. Deliberately *not* distinguishing them in the message: telling an unauthenticated caller whether their signature was wrong or merely stale is free reconnaissance.

I have not applied this — say the word and I will.

## Blast radius

| Route | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| All 8 `ArticleModule` guarded routes, `GET/PUT /user`, `POST/DELETE /profiles/:username/follow` | 500 | **401** |
| `GET /profiles/:username` (public, optional auth) | 500 | **401** |

- **No data is wrong.** This is a status-code translation bug on a read path — nothing is written, nothing was persisted incorrectly, no backfill is needed. What *is* wrong is client-side state: mobile installs have been treating a dead token as a server outage and holding onto it instead of clearing it. Those clients heal on the next request once they get a real 401 — no server-side remediation.
- **Judgement call to confirm:** `GET /profiles/:username` is optional-auth, so an expired token there could arguably be treated as anonymous (200, `following: false`) rather than 401. I chose 401 because it matches the rule recorded in `LESSONS.md:36` and because silently degrading to anonymous is what hides a dead token from the app in the first place. A caller sending *no* token is unaffected — `user.decorator.ts:14` guards that and returns `undefined` as before.
- `src/shared/base.controller.ts:12` is left alone as unreachable dead code. Flagging rather than fixing: if anyone ever extends `BaseController`, it reintroduces this exact 500. Worth deleting, but that's a separate change.

## How to verify

1. **Reproduce first.** Mint a token whose `exp` is in the past (temporarily flip `+ 60` to `- 1` at `src/user/user.service.ts:106`, register a user, grab the token, revert the line), then:
   ```
   curl -i -H "Authorization: Token <expired>" http://localhost:3000/api/user
   ```
   Expect `500` before the patch, `401` after. Remember the `/api` global prefix (`src/main.ts:8`).
2. **Tampered token** — flip one character in the signature: also `401`, not `500`.
3. **Public optional-auth route** — same expired token against `GET /api/profiles/<username>`: `401` after the patch; with **no** `Authorization` header at all it must still return `200`. That last one is the regression this change could plausibly break, so don't skip it.
4. **Valid token still works** — `GET /api/user` with a fresh token returns the `UserRO` envelope. Confirms `verifyToken` returns the decoded payload unchanged on the happy path.

Files I read: `auth.middleware.ts`, `user.decorator.ts`, `base.controller.ts`, `main.ts`, the three `*.module.ts` `configure()` blocks, `profile.controller.ts`, and `user.service.ts:95-128`. I did not read `src/config.ts` — it is not in the working tree (only `src/config.ts.example`), so `SECRET`'s value is unverified here; irrelevant to this bug, but it means the app won't compile as checked out.

Likely category: security — Auth / permission question: trace the enforcement point and assume the caller is hostile.

### [CURRENT_FOCUS.md] CURRENT_FOCUS.md > CURRENT FOCUS — RealWorld API (NestJS)
> Living doc. What is actually in flight right now. Read after LESSONS.md.

### [CURRENT_FOCUS.md] CURRENT_FOCUS.md > CURRENT FOCUS — RealWorld API (NestJS) > Active now
- [ ] **Spec conformance pass** — make article responses match the RealWorld spec: produce
      `favorited` per current user, rename `favoriteCount` → `favoritesCount` and
      `created/updated` → `createdAt/updatedAt` at the response boundary (not in the DB).
- [ ] **Ownership checks** on `PUT/DELETE /articles/:slug` and `DELETE /articles/:slug/comments/:id`
      — return 403 when the caller is not the author. Design first; the comment case needs a
      `comment.author` relation that does not exist yet.
- [ ] **Password change path** — hash on update (see LESSONS.md #88) and stop the raw body
      being merged into the entity.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > An invalid token must be a 401, not a 500 (#79)
**What happened:** an expired or tampered token made `jwt.verify()` throw inside
`AuthMiddleware.use()` (and inside the `@User()` decorator on public routes). Nothing caught it,
so the client got `500 Internal Server Error` and the mobile app treated it as an outage instead
of logging the user out.

**Rule:** wrap `jwt.verify` and translate its errors to `HttpStatus.UNAUTHORIZED`. A guard that
can crash is a guard that leaks framework errors.

### [.claude/knowledge/auth.md] auth.md > Authentication and authorization > Two ways a request learns who the user is > 1. `AuthMiddleware` — `src/user/auth.middleware.ts` (the guard)
Applied **per route, per module**, in each module's `configure(consumer)`. Behaviour:
- no `Authorization` header, or nothing after the space → `HttpException('Not authorized.', 401)`
- header present → `jwt.verify(token, SECRET)` → `userService.findById(decoded.id)` → sets
  `req.user = user.user` and calls `next()`.
- `jwt.verify` **throws** on an expired, malformed or wrongly-signed token, and nothing in the
  middleware catches it — the framework turns that into a **500**, not a 401 (see `LESSONS.md`).
- `findById` throws `HttpException({errors}, 401)` if the id no longer exists.

### [.claude/knowledge/auth.md] auth.md > Authentication and authorization > Two ways a request learns who the user is > 2. `@User()` decorator — `src/user/user.decorator.ts` (optional identity, no guard)
Used as `@User('id')`, `@User('email')`, or bare `@User()` on handler parameters.
- If the middleware ran, returns `req.user[data]` (or the whole user).
- Otherwise it decodes the token itself with `jwt.verify` and returns `decoded[data]` — so a
  route that is NOT in the middleware list can still see who is calling **if** a token is
  sent, and gets `undefined` if none is. (Bare `@User()` on an unguarded route returns
  `decoded.user`, which does not exist in the payload → `undefined`.)
- Same `jwt.verify` throw → 500 problem as the middleware.

### [.claude/knowledge/auth.md] auth.md > Authentication and authorization > The token
- Issued by `UserService.generateJWT(user)` (`src/user/user.service.ts`): payload
  `{ id, username, email, exp }`, signed with `SECRET` from `src/config.ts`, **expiry 60 days**.
- Returned inside the `UserRO` envelope on `POST /users` (register), `POST /users/login`, and
  `GET /user`.
- Sent by clients as `Authorization: Token <jwt>` (RealWorld convention). The code only ever
  reads `header.split(' ')[1]`, so `Bearer <jwt>` works too — the scheme word is ignored.

### [.claude/knowledge/auth.md] auth.md > Authentication and authorization > Which routes are guarded (from the three `configure()` blocks)
| Module | Guarded routes (401 without token) |
|---|---|
| `UserModule` | `GET /user`, `PUT /user` |
| `ArticleModule` | `GET /articles/feed` · `POST /articles` · `PUT /articles/:slug` · `DELETE /articles/:slug` · `POST /articles/:slug/comments` · `DELETE /articles/:slug/comments/:id` · `POST /articles/:slug/favorite` · `DELETE /articles/:slug/favorite` |
| `ProfileModule` | `profiles/:username/follow` for **all** methods (POST follow, DELETE unfollow) |

Everything else is **public**: `GET /articles`, `GET /articles/:slug`,
`GET /articles/:slug/comments`, `GET /profiles/:username`, `GET /tags`, `POST /users`,
`POST /users/login`, and — notably — **`DELETE /users/:slug`**, which deletes the user whose
*email* equals the `:slug` param (`UserService.delete(email)`), with no token required and no
check of who is asking.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > Never `Object.assign` a request body onto a persisted entity (#112)
**What happened:** `UserService.update()` and `ArticleService.update()` both merge the raw body
into the loaded entity. Any extra field the client sends — `id`, `password`, `authorId`,
`favoriteCount` — is persisted. The DTO type is a TypeScript annotation; it strips nothing at
runtime, and `PUT /user` / `PUT /articles/:slug` have no validation pipe.

**Rule:** copy the allowed fields by name, or whitelist with a validation pipe
(`whitelist: true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true`). The DTO class is not a filter.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > A relation that is not eager is `undefined`, not `[]`
**What happened:** `ArticleService.favorite()` loads the user with `findOne(id)` and then calls
`user.favorites.findIndex(...)`. `favorites` is a non-eager `@ManyToMany`, so it is `undefined`
→ `TypeError: Cannot read property 'findIndex' of undefined` → 500 on
`POST /articles/:slug/favorite`. Same pattern in `findAll()` for `?favorited=` (`author.favorites.map`).

**Rule:** before touching `entity.relation` in a service, find the `relations: [...]` or the
`eager: true` that loads it. If neither exists, the property is `undefined`.

### [.claude/knowledge/auth.md] auth.md > Authentication and authorization > Passwords
- Hashed by `UserEntity.hashPassword()` under `@BeforeInsert()` only.
- `UserService.update()` does `delete toUpdate.password` then `Object.assign(toUpdate, dto)`
  and saves. `UpdateUserDto` declares no `password` field, but nothing strips one from the
  request body, and `PUT /user` has no validation pipe.
- Login: `UserService.findOne({email, password})` → `argon2.verify(hash, password)`; unknown
  email or wrong password both return `null` → controller throws `HttpException({errors}, 401)`.
- Registration duplicate → `400` with `{ message: 'Input data validation failed', errors }`.

### [.claude/knowledge/workspace.md] workspace.md > RealWorld API (NestJS) — workspace overview > Conventions (these are the rules, not suggestions) > The response envelope and the `RO` suffix
`RO` means **Response Object**. Every controller method returns the RealWorld envelope, named
`<Thing>RO` in `*.interface.ts`:

| Endpoint family | Returns | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| single article | `ArticleRO` | `{ article: {...} }` |
| list | `ArticlesRO` | `{ articles: [...], articlesCount: n }` |
| comments | `CommentsRO` | `{ comments: [...] }` |
| user | `UserRO` | `{ user: {..., token} }` |
| profile | `ProfileRO` | `{ profile: {..., following} }` |

The frontends read `response.article.slug`, `response.user.token`, etc. A method that returns a
bare entity instead of the envelope breaks every RealWorld client (see `LESSONS.md`).

### [.claude/knowledge/workspace.md] workspace.md > RealWorld API (NestJS) — workspace overview > Conventions (these are the rules, not suggestions) > Request bodies are nested too
Handlers read `@Body('article')`, `@Body('user')`, `@Body('comment')` — the client sends
`{ "article": {...} }`, never a flat object. New endpoints follow the same nesting.

### [.claude/knowledge/workspace.md] workspace.md > RealWorld API (NestJS) — workspace overview > Stack
| Layer | Choice |
|---|---|
| Framework | NestJS 7 (`@nestjs/common` ^7.0.5) |
| ORM | TypeORM 0.2.24, `synchronize: true` (tables are created from entities on boot — there are NO migration files) |
| Database | MySQL (`ormconfig.json`) |
| Auth | JSON Web Token via `jsonwebtoken`, secret in `src/config.ts` (copied from `config.ts.example`) |
| Password hashing | `argon2` |
| Validation | `class-validator` + a hand-written `ValidationPipe` in `src/shared/pipes/validation.pipe.ts` |
| API docs | Swagger at `/docs` |
| Tests | Jest (`jest.json`); only `src/tag/tag.controller.spec.ts` exists |

Global prefix is `api` (`src/main.ts` → `app.setGlobalPrefix('api')`), so every route below is
really `/api/...`. Server listens on 3000.
</workspace_context>
